title: Two eyes on the smoke
topic: Across the Texas Panhandle, after the Smokehouse Creek fire, Xcel Energy and Pano AI put AI camera stations on communication towers that sweep for smoke every minute, a human analyst checks each flag, two cameras triangulate the spot and Pano calls 911, while many alerts turn out to be nothing.
hook: How do two towers pin one fire?

treatment.logline: After the largest wildfire in Texas history, a Panhandle tower watches the grass with two round camera eyes, and the film opens its job one step at a time: sweep, flag, human check, two sightlines crossing, the 911 call, and the alert that turns out to be nothing.
treatment.cold_open: A huge Panhandle sky over red dirt and tan grass. The camera station's two round heads are already turning on their tower. A thin grey curl rises at the horizon, and before second three both eyes stop and lock onto it while a rancher at a stock tank looks back over his shoulder.
treatment.turn: Other towers' alerts pour onto the firefighter's tablet and go grey as nothing, a dust devil, field dust, while the real curl's card stays orange. Xcel itself warns responders many alerts will be nothing, the cameras over towns pixelate what is built, and the bill is paid up front and headed to regulators.
treatment.button: A firefighter hoses the last of the curl into a wet black patch. The tower's two eyes blink and start another sweep. None of it puts out a fire. It buys a head start, and somebody still drives toward the smoke.

hero.name: the camera station with two eyes
hero.why: a lattice communication tower whose two round white camera heads are its two eyes, with irises that pan and brows that narrow on smoke. No earlier film has drawn a wildfire camera station, and two cameras that triangulate are literally a pair of eyes.

states.state: a thin grey curl rising off the grass on the horizon
boxed in amber on the analyst's screen as possible smoke
an orange pin on the map where two sightlines cross
hosed out to a wet black patch while the tower sweeps on

fingerprint.pov: the tower's own two eyes, then the people downstream of what they see
fingerprint.layout: cyan sightlines and beams crossing the tall frame on diagonals
fingerprint.hero_treatment: a lattice tower with two round white camera heads as eyes, cyan irises, brows that narrow
fingerprint.palette: Rolling Plains red dirt and tan grass under a big blue sky, cyan camera beams, one orange accent for the smoke pin

scenes.vo: A thin curl of smoke rises off the Panhandle grass. Up on a tower, two cameras turn and lock onto it.

draw.subject: the smoke curl
draw.action: rises off the far grass as the tower's two camera eyes swing toward it
draw.emotion: the rancher at the stock tank turns to look

draw.subject: the two camera eyes
draw.action: stop dead and narrow on the curl as a cyan beam shoots out to it

scenes.vo: There is a reason they are up there. The Smokehouse Creek fire started in Hutchinson County near Stinnett and became the largest wildfire in state history.

draw.subject: a black burn scar
draw.action: spreads outward from a pin near Stinnett across a county map

draw.subject: an orange pin
draw.action: drops onto Stinnett and the scar starts eating outward from it

draw.subject: the rancher
draw.action: kneels and rests a hand on a charred fence post

scenes.vo: It burned roughly 1,058,482 acres. Xcel Energy said its facilities appeared to have been involved.

draw.subject: black squares
draw.action: tile across the plains behind the rancher as a counter rolls up

draw.subject: the acre counter
draw.action: slams to a stop and the rancher folds his arms

draw.subject: a lineworker
draw.action: looks up at a power line strung over burned ground and grips her helmet brim

scenes.vo: So Xcel teamed up with a company called Pano AI. By last November, there were 57 camera stations across the Panhandle, each on top of a communication tower.

draw.subject: the lineworker
draw.action: bolts the last camera head onto the tower top and both eyes blink awake

draw.subject: the two camera heads
draw.action: blink open and look around as the lineworker throws her arms up

draw.subject: 57 tower dots
draw.action: pop up one after another across a Panhandle map as a counter climbs

scenes.vo: Each station sweeps a full 360 degrees every minute. It watches about 10 miles in each direction.

draw.subject: the tower's gaze
draw.action: sweeps round like a second hand over a clock face drawn on the prairie

draw.subject: a cyan ring
draw.action: draws itself on the ground far out while the rancher on horseback rides inside it
draw.emotion: the rancher looks up at the tower

scenes.vo: Its AI is hunting one thing. Smoke. When it finds a grey smudge on the horizon, it flags it.

draw.subject: the camera's view
draw.action: pans across grass, fence line and a far mesa

draw.subject: a grey smudge
draw.action: curls up off the far grass in the camera's view

draw.subject: an amber box
draw.action: snaps around the grey curl and the camera eyes widen

scenes.vo: A flag is not a fire, though. So a human analyst checks it first.

draw.subject: the analyst
draw.action: leans in toward the screen and pushes up her glasses

draw.subject: the amber box
draw.action: turns green with a tick as the analyst clicks

scenes.vo: Then a second tower turns its eyes the same way. Where the two sightlines cross, the map can get exact coordinates.

draw.subject: a second tower on the far ridge
draw.action: swings both eyes left as its beam reaches for the curl

draw.subject: two dashed beams
draw.action: cross on the map and an orange pin drops and bounces where they meet

scenes.vo: Pano calls 911. The closest fire department gets the live stream, and a brush truck rolls.

draw.subject: the call taker
draw.action: grabs the ringing phone and stands up

draw.subject: the brush truck
draw.action: pulls out with lights flashing and dust kicking while a firefighter holds up the stream on a tablet

scenes.vo: Here is the catch. Xcel's Reeves warns responders that a lot of these alerts will turn out to be nothing.

draw.subject: a dust devil
draw.action: spins across a farmer's field under another tower's beam and an alert box snaps onto it
draw.emotion: the farmer squints at it and scratches his head

visual_events.label: Many turn out to be nothing

draw.subject: the firefighter
draw.action: swipes grey nothing alerts off her tablet while the orange curl card stays put

scenes.vo: Most people are okay with that, he says. They want to know everything that is going on.

draw.subject: alert cards
draw.action: pile up on the firehouse table and most of them fade to grey
draw.emotion: the firefighter blows out a breath

draw.subject: the firefighter
draw.action: nods, pulls on her helmet and grabs the tablet off the hook

scenes.vo: Some cameras look over towns, though. Those pixelate anything built, houses and all.

draw.subject: the camera's gaze
draw.action: slides across a small town and its water tower while a resident looks up from her yard

draw.subject: the rooftops
draw.action: dissolve into blurry pixel blocks while the tower squeezes its eyes half shut as if minding its manners

scenes.vo: Somebody pays for all of it. Xcel paid up front and will ask regulators to recover that cost, and it planned 68 more under a $490 million resiliency plan.

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: turns over her power bill at the kitchen table and finds a NOT YET stamp

draw.subject: 68 new towers
draw.action: rise one after another along a Panhandle road toward the horizon

draw.subject: a coin stack
draw.action: rises beside the map and lands with a thud

scenes.vo: None of it puts out a fire. It buys a head start, and then somebody still has to drive toward the smoke.

draw.subject: the firefighter
draw.action: sprays the last of the curl and it hisses out into a wet black patch

draw.subject: the last flame
draw.action: hisses into a puff of white steam over the black patch

draw.subject: the brush truck
draw.action: drives off toward a new curl on the horizon while the tower's two eyes start another sweep
